## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Luóyún rěnrǔ jīng* (T500) is a one-fascicle short sūtra translated by the Western Jìn monk [法炬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%82%AC) Fǎjù (fl. 290–306 CE). The protagonist *Luóyún* 羅云 is Rāhula, the Buddha's son. The text is a teaching on *kṣānti* (forbearance, patience) given by Rāhula.

**Abstract**

This is one of about 30 short Hīnayāna sūtras translated by Fǎjù, often in collaboration with [法立](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%AB%8B) Fǎlì (the two are sometimes confused). The text portrays Rāhula as the model practitioner of *kṣānti pāramitā* — the Mahāyāna sixth perfection of forbearance. Fǎjù's translation career is dated to the *Yuánkāng* 元康 to *Yǒngxīng* 永興 reign-eras (290–306 CE).
